sections.content: You're in the listing appointment. The seller asks, "So how much will I actually walk away with?"
You pull out a napkin. You scratch some numbers. You mumble about "rough estimates." You promise to email them "something more detailed later."
Congratulations—you just lost credibility in the most important moment of the listing appointment.
Why Net Sheets Matter (A Lot)

The seller net sheet is often the first professional document a seller sees from you. It sets the tone for your entire relationship. Get it wrong—or look unprepared—and you're fighting uphill for trust.
Sellers expect:

items: **Accuracy:** They want the real number, not a guess
**Speed:** Waiting 24 hours for numbers kills momentum

sections.content: Common Net Sheet Mistakes
1. Forgetting Major Deductions
Agent commission, title fees, prorated taxes, HOA dues, mortgage payoff, transfer taxes, staging credits—the list is long and easy to miss.
2. Using Outdated Tax Rates or Fees
Tax prorations change. Transfer fees vary by county. Using last year's numbers creates surprises.
3. Creating Ugly Documents
Excel spreadsheets with crossed-out cells and handwritten notes don't inspire confidence.
4. Taking Too Long
If you can't generate a net sheet during the appointment, you're losing to agents who can.
How to Nail Every Net Sheet
1. Prep Your Numbers
Know current local tax rates, typical title fees, and commission structures before every appointment.
2. Use Professional Tools
Branded, clean documents that you can generate instantly make you look like the expert you are.
3. Explain Every Line
Don't just hand over a number—walk them through it. Education builds trust.
4. Create Multiple Scenarios
Show net proceeds at different price points. "Here's what you net at $400K, $420K, and $440K."
5. Email It Instantly
Follow up before you leave the driveway. Speed wins listings.
The Bottom Line
The agent who can confidently say "Here's exactly what you'll net"—with a professional document to back it up—wins the listing. Every time.
